items.stem: A client has used a high-potency topical corticosteroid for a prolonged period and now has visibly thin skin with telangiectasia and striae. Which adverse effect is most consistent with these findings?

options.A: Hyperkeratosis with progressive skin thickening is the characteristic local toxicity of prolonged clobetasol use.
options.B: Dependent edema is the expected local adverse effect that produces striae and visible superficial vessels.
options.C: Lichenification is the typical corticosteroid-induced change caused by increased dermal collagen production.
options.D: Skin atrophy with striae and telangiectasia is consistent with local toxicity from prolonged use of a high-potency topical corticosteroid.

items.rationale: FDA labeling for high-potency topical corticosteroids such as clobetasol lists local adverse reactions including skin atrophy, striae, and telangiectasia, especially with prolonged or higher-potency use. These findings therefore represent local corticosteroid toxicity rather than a therapeutic effect.
items.locator: Warnings/Adverse Reactions — local corticosteroid reactions including atrophy, striae, and telangiectasia.

items.stem: A reusable flexible bronchoscope has just been used for a client. Which reprocessing step is required before the bronchoscope is used again?

options.A: Meticulous cleaning followed by at least high-level disinfection is required before a reusable flexible bronchoscope is used again.
options.B: Low-level surface disinfection is adequate when the bronchoscope was used in a client without a known infection.
options.C: High-level disinfection can be performed effectively without prior cleaning of the bronchoscope channels.
options.D: Reprocessing the exterior surface is sufficient because internal channels do not contact mucous membranes.

items.rationale: CDC classifies heat-sensitive flexible endoscopes such as bronchoscopes as devices that must be properly cleaned and, at minimum, undergo high-level disinfection after each use. Meticulous cleaning is necessary before high-level disinfection or sterilization.
items.locator: Flexible bronchoscopes require cleaning and at least high-level disinfection after each use

items.stem: A nurse is handling contaminated linen. Which action is appropriate?

options.A: Sort contaminated linen in the client room before bagging so heavily soiled pieces can be separated early.
options.B: Handle contaminated linen with minimum agitation and contain it at the point of use, using leak-resistant containment when indicated.
options.C: Shake contaminated linen before bagging to remove loose material and reduce the laundry load.
options.D: Prerinse contaminated linen in the patient-care area before placing it in the transport container.

items.rationale: CDC recommends minimum agitation of contaminated textiles, containment at the point of use, no sorting or prerinsing in patient-care areas, and leak-resistant containment when textiles are contaminated with blood or body substances.

items.locator: Minimum agitation, point-of-use containment, and leak-resistant bags when indicated

items.stem: A dressing is saturated with blood and would release blood if compressed. How should this item be classified for disposal?

options.A: Classify it as sharps waste because any item containing visible blood belongs in a puncture-resistant sharps container.
options.B: Classify it as pharmaceutical waste because blood-contaminated material is disposed through the medication-waste stream.
options.C: Classify the dressing as regulated waste because it would release blood in a liquid or semiliquid state if compressed.
options.D: Classify it as ordinary solid waste because dressings are excluded from regulated waste regardless of saturation.

items.rationale: OSHA defines regulated waste to include contaminated items that would release blood or other potentially infectious material in a liquid or semiliquid state if compressed. The stem was narrowed from the vague phrase 'blood-soaked' to the regulatory criterion that determines classification.
items.locator: Definition of regulated waste under 29 CFR 1910.1030(b)

items.stem: A healthcare employee has occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious material. Which vaccine must the employer make available at no cost under OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard?

options.A: Make seasonal influenza vaccination available at no cost because it is the vaccine specified by the Bloodborne Pathogens Standard.
options.B: Make MMR vaccination available because it is the required postexposure vaccine for occupational blood exposure.
options.C: Make Tdap vaccination available because it is the vaccine OSHA specifically mandates for bloodborne-pathogen exposure.
options.D: Make hepatitis B vaccination available at no cost to employees with occupational exposure, subject to the standard’s stated exceptions.

items.rationale: 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires the employer to make hepatitis B vaccination available to employees with occupational exposure and to provide it at no cost. The standard includes exceptions such as prior completion of the series, demonstrated immunity, or medical contraindication.
items.locator: Paragraph 1910.1030(f): hepatitis B vaccination and no-cost requirement

items.stem: Which combination represents the CDC hierarchy used in a tuberculosis infection-control program for healthcare settings?

options.A: Use a hierarchy of administrative measures, environmental controls, and respiratory protective equipment for healthcare TB infection control.
options.B: Use contact precautions, surgical hand antisepsis, and environmental surface disinfection as the three levels of TB control.
options.C: Use staff antibiotic prophylaxis, ultraviolet exposure, and elimination of symptom screening as the three control levels.
options.D: Use standard precautions alone, because a separate respiratory-protection component is not part of healthcare TB control.

items.rationale: CDC describes a three-level hierarchy for healthcare TB infection control: administrative measures, environmental controls, and respiratory protective equipment. Administrative measures are the first and most important level and include prompt recognition and management of people with suspected infectious TB.
items.locator: Three-level hierarchy: administrative measures, environmental controls, respiratory protective equipment

items.stem: Which statement best distinguishes a fit-tested N95 filtering facepiece respirator from a surgical mask in a healthcare respiratory-protection context?

options.A: A surgical mask provides a tighter face seal than an N95 and is preferred for inhalation protection from airborne TB.
options.B: A fit-tested N95 is a tight-fitting respirator designed to filter airborne particles; a surgical mask does not provide the same fitted respiratory protection.
options.C: An N95 and a surgical mask provide equivalent filtration and fit when both are worn correctly.
options.D: An N95 is intended for splash protection but does not filter small airborne particles.

items.rationale: NIOSH-approved N95 filtering facepiece respirators are designed to filter airborne particles and must fit the wearer's face adequately as part of a respiratory-protection program. Surgical masks are loose-fitting source-control/barrier devices and do not provide the same fitted respiratory protection.
items.locator: Respirators versus facemasks: N95 filtering facepiece respirators require an adequate seal and provide fitted particulate respiratory protection.

items.stem: Environmental-services staff are performing terminal cleaning of a room that was managed under Contact Precautions. Which PPE is appropriate for the cleaning task?

options.A: Wear gloves alone because clothing protection is unnecessary once the client has left the room.
options.B: Wear a surgical mask and eye protection without gloves because Contact Precautions apply only while the client is present.
options.C: Wear a gown or protective apron and gloves appropriate for terminal cleaning in a Contact Precautions environment.
options.D: Wear an N95 respirator without gown or gloves because airborne protection replaces contact-barrier PPE during terminal cleaning.

items.rationale: CDC environmental-cleaning guidance lists gown/apron and reusable gloves for routine and terminal cleaning of areas under Contact Precautions. The original vague statement was narrowed to the PPE recommended for this specific cleaning task.

items.stem: A sharps container has reached its designated fill line. What should the nurse do?

options.A: Push the existing sharps downward with a tool to create room before replacing the container.
options.B: Transfer the contents into a larger sharps container so the original container can remain in service.
options.C: Continue using the container until the opening is physically blocked, then close and replace it.
options.D: Close and replace the sharps container at the designated fill line rather than allowing it to overfill.

items.rationale: OSHA requires sharps containers to be replaced routinely and not allowed to overfill. Containers must be closed immediately before removal or replacement, and reusable containers must not be manually opened or emptied in a way that exposes workers to percutaneous injury.
items.locator: §1910.1030(d)(4)(iii)(A)(2)(iii) sharps containers not allowed to overfill; §(A)(3)(i) close immediately before removal or replacement.

items.stem: A nurse practices outside the legal scope authorized by the applicable Nurse Practice Act. Which consequence is possible?

options.A: Board-of-nursing discipline is possible and may include remediation, restrictions, suspension, or revocation depending on law and the facts.
options.B: The consequence is limited to employer counseling because Nurse Practice Acts are not enforced by boards of nursing.
options.C: A scope violation automatically produces permanent license revocation regardless of severity or jurisdiction.
options.D: A scope violation automatically produces a criminal conviction before any regulatory investigation occurs.

items.rationale: Boards of nursing enforce Nurse Practice Acts to protect the public. NCSBN describes disciplinary actions that may include remediation, restrictions, suspension, or revocation; the exact sanction depends on state law and the facts of the case.
items.locator: Board disciplinary actions may restrict practice, suspend a license, or revoke/surrender a license
